title: Direct wastewater RNA extraction via MoS method
author: Oscar N Whitney
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.biwfkfbn
materials: Prepare 1 L each of two wash buffers - Wash buffer #1 (4S-WB1) and #2 (4S-WB2), for later use during cleanup of RNA bound to silica particles. Prepare a "Milk of Silica" suspension of dry silica.
Agitate sample to mix ethanol and wastewater lysate.
Prepare 1 L each of two wash buffers - Wash buffer #1 (4S-WB1) and #2 (4S-WB2), for later use during cleanup of RNA bound to silica particles. Prepare a "Milk of Silica" suspension of dry silica.

steps.title: Prepare 4S‑WB1 buffer
steps.instruction: In a sterile bottle add 490 mL water, 300 mL 5 M NaCl, 200 mL 100 % ethanol and 10 mL 1 M Tris (pH 7.2); agitate until fully mixed.

steps.title: Prepare 4S‑WB2 buffer
steps.instruction: In a sterile bottle add 170 mL water, 20 mL 5 M NaCl, 800 mL 100 % ethanol and 10 mL 1 M Tris (pH 7.2); agitate until fully mixed.

steps.title: Collect wastewater sample
steps.instruction: Obtain 40 mL wastewater in a sterile collection tube, keep at 4 °C during transport, and add NaCl and TE buffer (see step 4) immediately after collection.

steps.title: Spike recovery control
steps.instruction: Add a known volume and titer of bovine coronavirus (bCoV, Merck Animal Health Catalog #16445) to the 40 mL sample, then agitate to mix. (Other controls such as Phi6, OC43, or purified RNAs may be used.)

steps.title: Add NaCl and TE buffer
steps.instruction: Add 9.5 g NaCl to the 40 mL wastewater, prepare pH 7.2 TE buffer (1 M Tris, 100 mM EDTA) and add 400 µL TE buffer to the sample; vortex to dissolve.

steps.title: Optional heat inactivation
steps.instruction: Heat the sample at 70 °C for 30 min (00:30:00).

steps.title: Filter sample (5 µm PVDF)
steps.instruction: Filter the sample through a 5‑µm PVDF filter using either a 47‑mm reusable filter holder with Durapore® 5.0 µm membrane (Catalog #SVLP04700) in a Swinnex holder (Catalog #SX0004700) or a 300 mL magnetic funnel (Catalog #4242).

steps.title: Aliquot filtrate and add ethanol
steps.instruction: Divide the 40 mL filtrate into two 20 mL aliquots; to each add 20 mL 70 % ethanol (v/v). The filtrate should appear semi‑clear.

steps.title: Prepare Milk of Silica
steps.instruction: Resuspend 5 g silicon dioxide powder (≈99 % SiO₂, particle size 0.5‑10 µm, ~80 % 1‑5 µm; Catalog #SIGMA S5631) in 5 mL pure water to make a 1 g/mL slurry; invert 10 times. Scale to 5 mL per wastewater sample.

steps.title: Add silica slurry to aliquots
steps.instruction: Add 2.5 mL of the 1 g/mL Milk of Silica slurry to each 40 mL lysate‑ethanol aliquot, invert 10 times and incubate at room temperature for 10 min (00:10:00) to bind RNA to silica.

steps.title: Centrifuge and discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge tubes at 4000 × g, 4 °C, 5 min; discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Combine silica pellets
steps.instruction: Pour the silica suspension from one tube into the other so that both silica pellets are in a single tube.

steps.title: Wash with 4S‑WB1
steps.instruction: Add 20 mL 4S‑WB1 (Wash buffer #1) to the combined silica pellet, vortex until the pellet appears milky.

steps.title: Centrifuge and discard wash
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 4000 × g, 4 °C, 5 min; discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Wash with 4S‑WB2
steps.instruction: Add 20 mL 4S‑WB2 (Wash buffer #2) to the silica pellet, vortex until milky.

steps.title: Centrifuge and discard second wash
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 4000 × g, 4 °C, 5 min; discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Elute RNA from silica
steps.instruction: Resuspend the silica‑RNA pellet in 20 mL RNase‑free water pre‑warmed to 37 °C, vortex, and incubate at room temperature for 10 min (00:10:00).

steps.title: Remove excess wash buffer
steps.instruction: Vacuum‑aspirate any remaining 4S‑WB2 or incubate at room temperature for 10 min (00:10:00) to evaporate residual buffer.

steps.title: Separate eluate from silica
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 4000 × g, 37 °C, 5 min; transfer the aqueous supernatant to a new sterile conical tube for further concentration.

steps.title: Precipitate RNA with isopropanol
steps.instruction: To the eluate add 20 mL 100 % isopropanol and 4 mL 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.2); invert 10 times and incubate at room temperature for 10 min (00:10:00).

steps.title: Pellet nucleic acids
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 4000 × g, 4 °C, 1 hour; a semi‑translucent nucleic‑acid pellet forms at the tube bottom.

steps.title: Decant isopropanol and water
steps.instruction: Carefully decant and discard the excess isopropanol‑water mixture without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Wash pellet with 75 % ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 40 mL 75 % ethanol, invert/vortex until the pellet loosens, then centrifuge at 5000 rpm, 4 °C, 5 min.

steps.title: Remove ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Aspirate the supernatant (70 % ethanol) with a small‑opening tip, then incubate the tube at 37 °C for 10 min (00:10:00) to evaporate residual ethanol.

steps.title: Re‑precipitate nucleic acid
steps.instruction: Centrifuge again at 4000 × g, 4 °C, 30 min; the pellet becomes clearly visible.

steps.title: Final ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Decant supernatant, add 1 mL 70 % ethanol, resuspend the pellet in 1 mL 75 % ethanol, and transfer the mixture to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube (cut the tip of a 1 mL pipette tip to facilitate transfer).

steps.title: Resuspend in water or TE
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 200 µL RNase‑free water or TE buffer, vortex; if silica particles remain, briefly centrifuge and transfer the clear supernatant to a new sterile 1.5 mL tube.

steps.title: Dissolve residual NaCl
steps.instruction: Vortex or shake the original sample for 30 seconds (00:00:30) to ensure all NaCl is dissolved.

steps.title: Store extracted RNA
steps.instruction: Store the purified RNA at 4 °C for same‑day use or at –80 °C for long‑term storage.
